clue.text: Embodiment of male reserve gets shot

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

explanation.surface: A personification of manly reticence ends up being shot, like a victim in a thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: A cock that is shy would be the very embodiment of male reserve. A cockshy is a fairground throw at a target, so the answer can mean a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockshy is a throw or try at hitting a target at a fair, hence a shot in the sense of an attempt.

clue.text: Model way to be unaccompanied in Kipling's story

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the runway along which fashion models parade

definitions.text: to be unaccompanied in Kipling's story
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what the cat does in Kipling's Just So story, The Cat that Walked by Himself

explanation.surface: A route for a role model, recalled alongside a solitary figure in a Kipling tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Just So Stories include The Cat that Walked by Himself, so a lone walk in that story is a cat walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A catwalk is the raised runway where fashion models show clothes; split in two it describes the cat's solitary walk.

clue.text: Prisoners at play?

parts.note: setter's reading: theatregoers who cannot escape the performance they are watching

explanation.walkthrough: 'At play' suggests games in a prison yard, but it means attending a play; the people watching are held there like prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes listeners or spectators who cannot leave, so are obliged to hear the speaker or show out.

clue.text: Accompaniment of 6 19, downy like a feather

parts.note: downy things are soft to the touch

explanation.surface: Something that goes with pleasant tunes, described as fluffy and feathery.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 19 is SWEET MUSIC; the old song 'Soft Lights and Sweet Music' pairs the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle low lamplight traditionally goes with sweet music in the romantic Irving Berlin song title.

clue.text: A lout, some say a hoodlum

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run lying across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of say, all of a and the start of hoodlum

explanation.surface: Some people call a thug a lout.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans sa(Y A HOO)dlum. A yahoo is a boor, from the brutish creatures in Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's Yahoos were brutish humans, so the word came to mean a coarse, uncouth person, a boor.

clue.text: Don't allow us to write in Black Hills state

indicators.note: the phrase is placed inside the state's postal abbreviation

parts.note: South Dakota, home of the Black Hills, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A ban on us writing in the Black Hills state of South Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: SD is the postal code for South Dakota, where the Black Hills and Mount Rushmore are.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend someone is to bar them temporarily from playing or working, refusing them permission for a while.

clue.text: Insolvent soldier raised to height — very touching!

parts.note: British slang for having no money

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word means reading it from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A penniless soldier gets promoted, a tale that is very moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very touching' looks like an emotional verdict on the story, but it is literal: clothes that touch the body all over.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin-tight garments cling closely to the body, pressing against it everywhere, in a literal sense of touching.

clue.text: Guardian entry into arranged course

indicators.note: one item enters another, so it sits within the second

parts.note: the editorial we used by a newspaper such as the Guardian

explanation.surface: A newspaper entry fitted into an organised series of lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: A newspaper's leader column speaks of the paper as 'we', the editorial plural.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a sweet is the dessert, a course of a meal served after the main dish.

clue.text: Flower (river) men settled with pigeons

indicators.note: the letters are settled into a new order, arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written; the parentheses pun on flower as something that flows

explanation.surface: Men by a river have settled there along with some pigeons.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a flower is often a river, as it flows; here the setter teases with that and then means a real flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening primrose is a plant with yellow blooms that open towards dusk, a genuine garden flower.

clue.text: Go off and do excavations in the matter of a ship

explanation.surface: Leave and carry out archaeological digging relating to a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to go off the subject, wandering away from the main topic in speech or writing.

clue.text: Lettuce's wrinkle? There's much more underneath

definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsically: a hint (wrinkle) belonging to the iceberg variety of lettuce
second meaning: the small visible part of a much larger hidden problem

explanation.surface: A crinkle on a salad leaf hides a great deal more below.
explanation.walkthrough: A wrinkle is an old word for a handy hint or tip; iceberg is a crisp lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a small visible sign of a far larger matter that remains hidden, as most of an iceberg floats submerged.

clue.text: Fairy's sign with pound for shilling

indicators.note: with one thing for another means swapping the first in where the second stood

parts.note: the ram, a sign of the zodiac
the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: A fairy's star sign, where pounds take the place of old shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: The S at the end of the zodiac sign is replaced by L; a shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, twenty to the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest, a sprite of the fairy kind.

clue.text: Having downed tools, down tools to hit harder

parts.note: workers who have downed tools are out
to down tools is to go on strike

explanation.surface: Workers who have walked out walk out again to put more force on employers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downed tools' and 'down tools' look like a repeated stutter, but each is a separate piece of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrike is to surpass someone in striking, delivering blows with more force than an opponent.

clue.text: Don't stop monarch entertaining another Poe, for example

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds that guest within
another version of a name is a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A king tells himself to keep going while hosting a second Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going means to continue or persevere, carrying on without stopping or halting.

clue.text: Purpose of being taut as reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by speech, so it is heard rather than seen

parts.note: something taut is held under strain

explanation.surface: Asking about the aim of keeping something tight, as people say.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is an aim or plan, what someone means to achieve by an action.

clue.text: Standard American's a sham

definitions.note: a noun phrase; the answer is usually an adjective, though it can mean a fake thing

parts.note: from bog-standard, British slang for ordinary

explanation.surface: An ordinary American turns out to be a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog-standard is British slang for plain or ordinary, so BOG stands for 'standard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bogus is counterfeit or fake, a pretence that passes itself off as genuine.

clue.text: Supporters like this and like greens

parts.note: Latin sic, thus, used to mark something quoted as written

explanation.surface: Fans who resemble each other and also like the colour green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests fans, but it is underwear that supports.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassicas are the cabbage family, including kale and sprouts, eaten as green vegetables.

clue.text: Excite love clad in reddish brown

indicators.note: something clad in a covering is wrapped around by it

parts.note: love is nil, a zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Stirring up romance dressed in auburn tones.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to stir up or rouse, getting someone moving or roused into action.

clue.text: Traitor finds Our Thing leaderless, which takes the biscuit

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Cosa Nostra, Italian for our thing, is the Mafia's name for itself

explanation.surface: An informer discovers the Mob is without its boss, which is the last straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the biscuit' sounds like an exclamation of outrage, but ratafia is drunk with or flavours a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is an almond liqueur, also the name of an almond biscuit, so it goes with or takes the form of a biscuit.

clue.text: Four-letter word causes great problem in public transport

indicators.note: the result sits inside the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a street railway vehicle

indicators.note: a problem leaves things in disorder, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone swears on a bus and causes a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: A four-letter word normally means an obscenity, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word made of four letters, from Greek tetra, four, and gramma, letter.

clue.text: Spots setter, one without sense, including the French

indicators.note: one thing including another holds it within

explanation.surface: Someone notices the crossword setter is a fool, with French involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Measles is the childhood illness whose main symptom is a red rash of blotches over the skin.

clue.text: Accompaniments of roast turkey on barbershop floor?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the traditional side dishes served with a festive roast
second meaning: the bits of hair cut off and swept up

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a playful one: what lies on the floor after haircuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimmings are both the usual extras with a Christmas roast and the cut-off pieces left after trimming hair.

clue.text: Notes sound on 1 down, say, almost unfit

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short of its final letter
say asks us to voice the noise, then spell what we hear differently

parts.note: the noise a cat makes; the cat comes from the earlier answer, and a Greek letter is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A sickly noise heard on the model runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is CATWALK, whose cat mews; the Greek letter mu is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is made of notes, so the plural noun stands for the art of musical sound.

clue.text: Watch fifth change to second seal

indicators.note: one letter is changed to another, swapped in its place

parts.note: a vigil is a night watch
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Instructions to adjust a watch from the fifth setting to the second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' and 'second' suggest a timepiece, but the watch is a vigil.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigil is a seal or signet, or a symbol thought to have magical power.

clue.text: Graduate's back with another dance

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: a Master of Arts, with the possessive s
another graduate, an American Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A graduate returns to the floor with a different dance partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Both degrees are reversed: an MA's and an AB, the American form of BA.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian ballroom dance in two-four time, linked to Carnival.

clue.text: Refinery, as it were, in … in trying to catch … a lot of fish

indicators.note: the first word goes in, placed inside the next piece

parts.note: angling is trying to catch fish
a school is a shoal of fish

explanation.surface: A broken sentence about going fishing for a big haul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it were' marks the definition as playful: a finishing school refines young women's manners rather than oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A finishing school polishes young people's social graces, so it is jokingly a place where people are refined.

clue.text: French town — here lace beer at sergeant's direction

parts.note: a sergeant is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: In a French town lace and beer are produced on a sergeant's orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here lace' is an aside: the town gives its name to Alençon lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Alençon is a town in Normandy, famous for its needlepoint lace.

clue.text: Not so many letters from canal builder

explanation.surface: Fewer letters arriving from the engineer who built a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: Ep. is the abbreviation for an epistle, a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand de Lesseps was the French diplomat who developed the Suez Canal.
